I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life, and my father before me. At 53, I'm not going to try anything risky. This county is wheat-and-corn country — everyone knows it, the grain stations buy it, and the soil suits it. I have about 10 mu. My neighbors who rented out their land and went to the city — some are doing fine, some regret it. I'm staying.

The plan is simple: winter wheat this autumn, then summer maize on the same ground right after the wheat harvest in June. Same rotation my family has done for decades. I'll use the improved wheat variety the township agricultural station has been promoting — better yield and it handles the rust better than the old seeds. For maize I'll use hybrid seed, same as last five years. Zhengdan 958 or whatever the seed shop has that's similar. Hybrids are the only thing worth planting for maize now.

For fertilizer — I apply a compound base fertilizer at planting, then top-dress with urea. I know the government says we over-apply nitrogen, but I'd rather see a strong crop than lose yield trying to cut back. I've seen what happens when you under-fertilize.

Water is the concern every year. We have the electric pump and the well hasn't run dry yet. For wheat I water three times — the winter water before it gets cold, the jointing water in spring, and once more at heading. Maize depends on rain, but I'll water twice to be safe.

Pest and disease I spray twice per crop. Wheat gets an herbicide pass in winter and a fungicide spray at heading. Maize gets treated for corn borer and I spot-spray if I see anything else.

I do rotary tillage before planting wheat. For maize I go directly into the stubble — no-tillage, saves diesel and time.
